lead.title: vLLM 0.29.0 makes Model Runner V2 the default for all models
lead.summary: The latest vLLM release turns Model Runner V2 into the default everywhere and adds support for Hy4-preview, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, GraniteSWA/MoeSWA and NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3. It also ships major Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 kernel optimizations plus expanded speculative decoding (DSpark, MTP, sparse MLA). For anyone serving open-weight models locally, this is the most consequential runtime update of the day.

top_stories.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: brand-new MIT-licensed open-weight architecture family
top_stories.summary: DeepSeek released its smallest model in a new Causal Encoder-Decoder family: ~552B total / 8B active MoE with native multimodal understanding, up to 1M contextcars and roughly a quarter of the prior generation's KV-cache HBM. MIT weights are on the Hub and old v4-flash IDs now route to this model.

top_stories.title: Qualcomm's next Snapdragon chip sharpens its on-device AI push
top_stories.summary: Qualcomm detailed its next-generation Hexagon NPU: a new Element Accelerator for transformer workloads, 50% more shared memory, KV-cache acceleration, context support to 32Kcars and roughly 50% faster INT4 prefill than the current Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 — targeting 30B-parameter MoE models that activate only ~3B parameters on phones.

top_stories.title: Wiz finds 1 in 10 exposed LiteLLM gateways accept the default sk-1234 key
top_stories.summary: Wiz scanned 3,074 internet-exposed LiteLLM gateways and found 9.6% accept the default master key or no auth at all, chaining with the MCP auth bypass (CVE-2026-59822) and guardrail RCE (CVE-2026-59821) into root-level code execution and cloud credential theft. Rotate the master key and upgrade to LiteLLM 1.84.0+.

top_stories.title: Positron AI raises $875M Series C for AI inference hardware
top_stories.summary: Positron AI closed an $875M Series C co-led by NEA, Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners and others for its AI inference hardware platform — one of the largest recent bets on alternatives to NVIDIA for running models.

items.title: Online draft co-training for speculative decoding in long-context RL post-training
items.summary: NVIDIA's system enables online co-training of speculative drafts (EAGLE-3, DFlash, DSpark) by merging rank-local branch attention into packed zigzag-ring context-parallel attention, delivering 1.50–1.88x end-to-end roll-out speedups on targets up to 122B while preserving the RL trajectory.

items.title: Forward-free LLM depth pruning via weight redundancy
items.summary: Weight-Redundancy Pruning removes whole Transformer blocks without any forward passes, scoring inter-block similarity from weight redundancy instead of activation statistics — cutting inference cost while avoiding calibration-data forward passes entirely.

items.title: RiLM: parameter-efficient language modeling via geodesic decoding
items.summary: RiLM removes the output softmax matrix entirely for sub-million-parameter models by decoding over squared geodesic distance on a Riemannian manifold. HypRiLM, at ~290k params, reaches 54.2 validation perplexity on WikiText-2 versus 87.6 for the flat variant, aimed at edge deployment.

items.title: DiffLUT-Net: differentiable training of FPGA LUT networks
items.summary: An FPGA-native neural network built from six-input lookup tables with learnable connectivity, trained end-to-end via differentiable training rather than converting pretrained quantized models — eliminating multiply-accumulate operations in favor of LUT-based on-chip execution.

items.title: Readable schemas beat fixed keys for SLM vehicle-agent function calls
items.summary: A study under strict memory and latency constraints for on-device in-vehicle assistants shows readable natural-language schemas outperform fixed opaque keys for small-model function-call accuracy in resource-limited deployments.

items.title: IBM releases SOTA Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2 under a permissive license
items.summary: IBM Research's ~385M-parameter open-weight time-series foundation model is dual-licensed under Apache 2.0 and OpenMDW 1.0, and as of September 8 it tops GIFT-Eval among replicable zero-shot models under a permissive license.

items.title: AuK: open-source foundational model for speech generation and editing
items.summary: AK highlights the AuK technical report, an open-source foundational model for speech generation and editing, with the paper and weights hosted on Hugging Face.

items.title: NeoMME: efficient multimodal-native multilingual encoders (260M/800M)
items.summary: An encoder-only alternative to generative VLM backbones trained from scratch with masked discrete-diffusion over text and raw image patches. Apache 2.0 checkpoints ship with a visual-RAG retriever head for page-image document retrieval.

items.title: Qwen ZG: local-first semantic grep for AI agents
items.summary: Qwen's team open-sourced ZG, a local-first CLI fusing ripgrep, BM25 and vector search for intent-based code search. Qwen benchmarks report up to 58.6% fewer agent tool calls and up to 82.7% fewer input tokens on SWE-QA Bench and real repos like pylint.

items.title: Orchestrator: spawn and manage Claude Code instances remotely
items.summary: A Show HN open-source tool for spawning and remotely managing multiple Claude Code instances, aimed at teams running fleets of local coding agents.

items.title: almost-cli: BYOK multi-agent coding, local first
items.summary: A provider-agnostic CLI that runs a team of specialized agents (Architect, Planner, Builder, Tester, Debugger) locally against your codebase with your own API keys. MCP tools are permission-gated per tool with deny-by-default policies.

items.title: Kryzz AI v1.1: open-sourced local-first Android AI workspace
items.summary: Kryzz AI was open-sourced (MIT) as a private, local-first Android AI workspace for chat, voice and tool-driven agents. v1.1 adds MiniMax as a provider, a multi-step Agent Auto tool loop and starter skills.

items.title: Skillctl: audit context cost and conflicts across agent skills
items.summary: A Show HN CLI that audits context cost and conflicts across your agent skill definitions, helping local agent setups size and de-conflict their skill packs.

items.title: n8n ships 2.38.6 stable with memory-bound source-control push
items.summary: n8n's stable 2.38.6 bounds peak memory during source-control push, while 2.39.x pre-releases add fixes for the sandboxed built-in AI assistant (Instance AI), MCP tool handling and prevent Anthropic agent threads from breaking permanently.

items.title: Community evidence Qwen3.8 was post-trained on GPT-5.5 chain-of-thought
items.summary: A community experiment prefilled 45 prompts per model with GPT-5.5 Pro reasoning and found Qwen3.8's answers became dramatically more GPT-5.5-like (+18.18pp) while other local models barely moved — strong evidence Qwen3.8 was trained on that reasoning data.

items.title: Single-GPU eval: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 vs Qwen3.8-27B FP8 for agent workloads
items.summary: A homelab user benchmarked Flash-Next NVFP4 against the 27B FP8 on a single RTX PRO 6000: Flash-Next was faster with flawlessly strict JSON and injection resistance, but denied partial credit on rubric-edge items where the 27B consistently complied.

items.title: Local-first AI is a systems problem, not a model problem
items.summary: A systems essay argues running local AI well is engineering, not model choice: unbounded concurrency against one local model causes requests to evict each other's KV memory, so bounded queues, visible streaming and deliberate memory planning are required for multi-agent homelabs.

items.title: A modder brings NVIDIA's unreleased RTX 3070 Ti 16GB to life
items.summary: Brazilian modder fmklab rebuilt the never-released RTX 3070 Ti 16GB by transplanting a 3070 Ti core onto an RTX 3070 PCB with GDDR6 chips, verifying the full 16GB pool by running a local LLM that used nearly all of it — a cheap path to more VRAM.

items.title: RTX 5070 reportedly getting a second variant on the larger GB203 die
items.summary: Leaker Hongxing2020 claims NVIDIA is preparing an RTX 5070 revision using the larger GB203 die instead of GB205, keeping core count, 12GB GDDR7 and the 192-bit bus — a supply-flex signal as Blackwell wafers get binned down-market.

items.title: Framework finds cheaper LPCAMM2 stock and immediately cuts prices
items.summary: Framework secured a limited batch of cheaper Micron 32GB and 64GB LPCAMM2 modules and is retroactively reducing memory prices for shipped and upcoming Laptop 13 Pro orders — a rare downward move in the RAM price crunch inflating local rig builds.

items.title: Radeon RX 9070 XT becomes AMD's most popular discrete GPU on Steam
items.summary: AMD's top-end RDNA 4 card overtook other AMD GPUs to become the most popular Radeon discrete card in Valve's Steam hardware survey, as NVIDIA RTX 50 supply stays constrained and street prices keep climbing.
